title: Budget impact and practice of extended community pharmacy opening: a convergent segregated mixed-methods systematic review
abstract: Objective: to synthesise evidence on the budget impact of extending community pharmacy opening into evenings and Sundays, and on how extended hours work in practice. Design: convergent segregated mixed-methods systematic review with a budget strand re-priced to 2026 and a practice-and-views strand synthesised thematically, integrated in a joint display. Primary outcomes: net budget impact for the payer shown across counterfactual assumptions; synthesised findings on access, staffing, safety and displacement. Results and conclusions will be written after the review.
introduction: Health authorities are asked to fund extended pharmacy opening on the strength of claimed savings. Existing costings depend on what users would otherwise have done, and the practicalities of late-night staffing are rarely costed.
methods: Searches of four bibliographic sources and grey literature from 2005; separate eligibility, extraction and appraisal for each strand; no meta-analysis because budget figures differ in perspective, price year and offsets. Confidence in practice findings is rated with GRADE-CERQual.
results: No data have been extracted yet. The report will present the flow of studies for each strand, the re-priced budget table, the thematic findings with confidence ratings, and the joint display.
discussion: The discussion will set the budget figures beside who uses late opening and what it costs to staff, and state what the evidence can and cannot tell the board.
limitations: Few comparable budget studies; counterfactual assumptions dominate; advocacy funding; grey literature of variable quality.
conclusion: To be written after the review; it will not report a pooled budget figure.
reportingChecklist: PRISMA 2020 with JBI mixed-methods guidance and CHEERS 2022 items for extracted economic data
summary: PRISMA-structured draft with two strands; results empty until extraction.
